newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Safras sees Brazil 96/97 soy crop at 26.02 mln tns.
newsitem.headline: Safras sees Brazil 96/97 soy crop at 26.02 mln tns.

text.p: Independent consultant Safras e Mercado said it was revising its forecast for Brazil's 1996/97 soybean crop down to 26.02 million tonnes from its most recent estimate of 26.22 million tonnes.

This was still a record and represented an eight percent increase on the 24.15 million tonnes harvested in 1995/96, Safras said. Planted area was 11.45 million hectares in 1996/97 and average productivity was record at 2,282 kilos per hectare.

The revision was mainly due to a sharp drop in the crop of key growing region Rio Grande do Sul following extended drought. Safras previously reduced its crop estimate to 26.22 million tonnes from an initial 26.88 million for the same reason.
"Soybean growers in Rio Grande do Sul will have to make do with a harvest of 4.8 million tonnes versus an initial forecast of up to six million tonnes," Safras said in a weekly report.

Brazilian growers increased planted area by five percent this year, favouring soybeans over corn, and also invested in productivity with a 15 percent increase in sales of fertilizers and pesticides, the report said.

"In any case, despite the fullsome harvest, the country will face problems in the composition of demand and supply tables, as exports of soybeans should reach much higher than expected levels," Safras said.

"The result is a year of distorted and paradoxal balance, given that despite hitting a new record in export revenue, (Brazil) will have to acquire large quantities of grain and subproducts to guarantee its internal supply," it added.

However, this might make good businees sense if the Chicago futures market drops as expected so that Brazilian producers and processors can sell when prices peak and buy when they bottom, Safras concluded.
